item.title: From Hive to Handmade: Wax Working, Honey and Hive Products Work — Sat Nov 7, 9:00 AM — E. L. Niño Bee Lab
item.description: What can you create from one of the most remarkable materials produced by honey bees? Join the California Master Beekeeper Program and Bee Haven Team at the E. L. Niño Bee Lab for a full day of hands-on learning, creativity, and discovery, led by certified CA master beekeeper and educator Catherine Hounshell alongside Dr. Elina Niño and her lab team. You’ll learn how bees make wax and how it functions in the colony, how beekeepers collect and safely clean and process beeswax, and how to turn it into handcrafted products you can make again at home. This is definitely not a workshop where you simply sit and listen. You’ll create molded beeswax candles, poured candles, and beeswax lip balm, and take home two of each item. All materials are provided. With the holidays just around the corner, the timing could not be better for handmade gifts. item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Sat Nov 7, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Sat Nov 7, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Above Bone — Sat Nov 7, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: ADERO WILLARD ABOVE BONE November 6–29, 2026 Reception and Artist Talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM Artist in the gallery on Sundays, November 8 and 29, 12–5 PM Axis Gallery presents Above Bone, an exhibition of ceramic sculpture by Sacramento artist Adero Willard, on view November 6 through 29, 2026. The exhibition brings together new work and pieces never before shown in Sacramento or on the West Coast. Join the artist for the reception and artist talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM. ABOUT THE EXHIBITION Above Bone refers to what is beneath, the layers, and what emerges. Clay sculptural vessels of heads and body forms explore death, regeneration, new growth, and what is hidden. Adero wrestles clay into expressive forms and creates surfaces dense in color and pattern: thick clay and delicately etched vines and flowers. The forms are camouflaged, as if growing from or being returned to the ground. Layered colorful patterns, resists, and luster build up over multiple firings. Pat

item.title: Capturing Memories of Grief/Capturando Memorias del Duelo — Sat Nov 7, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: SUMMER VENTIS AND LINA RINCÓN CAPTURING MEMORIES OF GRIEF/CAPTURANDO MEMORIAS DEL DUELO November 6–29, 2026 Reception on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM The project, “Capturing Memories of Grief,” is a collaboration between artist Summer Ventis, sociologist and poet Lina Rincón, and you. Together, we explore the intersection of grief, memory, and image. We began this project with a conversation about our shared experience of losing a parent. When we recalled these experiences, we learned that we both had memories that centered around images, photographs, and the process of photography as a way to make sense of and process the meanings of our loss. In Fall of 2025, we began a series of grief-themed tours of works in the Crocker Art Museum’s collection. At the end of the tours, participants gathered to share and document our memories of grief and loss and how they connect with different types of images. Explore cultural and artisan booths throughout I-House, enjoy food trucks out front, and experience a full lineup of performances on our backyard stage. It’s an open house in the truest sense: for the day, this is your house too, and every culture and community has a place here. item.description: A (post)Halloween costume party featuring Inner Nature, Roni Jean and Valley Taylor. Costume not required; but best costume wins a 3 band merch package! Inner Nature is the work of Casey Groat from Sacramento, CA. Having started out as just a kid with an interest in making noises with the computer, the project has matured into themes such as love and loss, as well as experimenting with sampling and songs with meaning and purpose. Artists such as Washed Out, Toro Y Moi, Small Black and Neon Indian are a big influence on the sound. Roni Jean carves out a unique niche with a blend of Haunted Indie Rock, Dreampop, and Shoegaze in Sacramento, CA. Their music weaves lush, dynamic soundscapes with a melodic melancholy that always carries an undeniable edge. Drawing inspiration from artists like Sir Chloe, Wisp, and Radiohead, Roni Jean moves seamlessly between moments of delicate vulnerability and explosive, powerful expression. item.title: Mean Girls The Musical — Fri Nov 6, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
November 6 through November 29, 2026 Cady Heron may have grown up on an African savanna, but nothing prepared her for the wild and vicious ways of her strange new home: suburban Illinois. How will this naïve newbie rise to the top of the popularity pecking order? By taking on The Plastics, a trio of lionized frenemies led by the charming but ruthless Regina George. But when Cady and her friends devise a “Revenge Party” to end Regina’s reign, she learns the hard way that you can’t cross a queen bee without getting stung. Recommended for ages 13 and up

Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Nov 25, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Sat Nov 14, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
